title: Chapter 2: Finally, the Stage of the Otome Game, the Royal Capital 1
content: Since defeating the magician controlling the Magic Bug, the outside of the mansion had transformed into a remarkably beautiful sight.
It had been such an overwhelming amount that it felt like a breath of fresh air.
By the way, thanks to Alicia starting gardening as a way to relieve stress, our home was now overflowing with greenery, making it look much nicer.
"It's a shame we can't harvest the radishes that grow in twenty days."
"Alicia-sama, I will deliver them to the academy as soon as they are ready."
"Can everyone in the mansion eat them? That's why I made them."
By the way, the gardening that could be called such was only a small part from the mansion's gate to the entrance, while the garden at the back was solely for vegetables.
Why did she suddenly start a home garden?
Do noble ladies who are no longer villains all become farmers?
At first, I had such questions, but it turned out she simply wanted to try everything she had never done before.
She wanted to experience things that she had previously overlooked due to her status, now that she was no longer a member of a duke's family but part of the Brave Family.
What a good girl, what a good girl.
"I can't eat it if you say it's okay for us to eat... it's too wasteful..."
"Ah, I would prefer if only the young master goes to the academy..."
"Alicia-sama can stay here at the mansion..."
"The servants are all very lonely... sniff sniff..."
All the mansion's servants had gathered around her with tears in their eyes, and she had become an indispensable presence in the Brave Family.
It's amazing; Alicia could handle everything, from cooking and laundry to cleaning, at the same level as the professional servants, aside from helping with work.
Of course, that makes sense, right?
In the Brave Territory, where there wasn't much to do, all the resources that had been devoted to the noble's higher education had been poured into household chores.
It's only natural that a hyper-domestic prodigy would emerge.
"School life is tough! If anything happens, please call for us immediately!"
"I'm fine. Since there's a shortage of personnel, I shouldn't overdo it, right? That's why I became capable of living alone."
"Alicia-sama, please rely on us anytime if anything happens!"
The conversations between the maidservants and Alicia were heartwarming, but I couldn't help but feel dissatisfied with the difference in treatment.
"Not a word for me, huh... Hahaha..."
Having been born and raised in this mansion, I was finally heading to the Royal Capital.
It was my first time outside the territory, aside from enemy countries, but why was that?
"Wow, I don't know how to ride a train? I'm scared?"
"Well, that's quite a childish thing to say."
"...Shut up."
I had tried to voice my desire for attention, but I felt embarrassed by Sebas's comment next to me, so I fell silent.
"Alicia-sama, please take care of the young master!"
"If anything happens, feel free to scold him right away!"
"He has a collar. It was put on him when he was little."
"A collar...? That's such a training method..."
Alicia was bewildered by the overly dramatic words of the servants.
It might sound like a joke, but he really had worn one.
Back then, I was a mischievous little brat who would eagerly venture into dangerous mountains, thinking, "Wow, this is another world, how exciting!"
"I'm sorry, Lagna. Did I keep you waiting?"
"No, it's fine, hahaha... haha..."
Alicia finally freed herself and rushed over to me and Sebas waiting in front of the carriage, firmly holding the collar, which made me let out a dry laugh.
"Young master! If anything happens to Alicia-sama, I won't forgive you!"
"If anything happens, it'll be coffee made from wrung-out rags!"
"I-I understand..."
Our servants were truly something else.
"You really are well-liked, huh? Hehe, I'm a little envious."
"Well, I guess... that's true."
When Alicia directed her innocent smile at me, I couldn't bring myself to say I was envious of how she was treated.
The bloodline of the Brave Family, always at the forefront, didn't particularly enjoy using others as pawns, so this was just fine.
"Now, let's go. Please get into the carriage."
At Sebas's voice, Alicia and I climbed into the carriage.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/ZJqPzj3.jpeg
Finally, we were heading to the Royal Capital, where the nobles gathered at the academy, the stage of our story.
I heard a slight sound next to me, like someone gulping nervously.
From the atmosphere surrounding Alicia, I could tell she was still harboring an indescribable anxiety about the academy.
No matter how bravely she tried to act, it was understandable since this was the epicenter of the trauma etched in her heart.
"Alicia, I have a pathetic request, but..."
"What is it?"
"When we arrive at the station, could you teach me how to buy a ticket and ride the train?"
"...Pfft."
At my pathetic request, she couldn't help but burst out laughing.
"Don't laugh at me!"
In a place I had never been, with infrastructure I had never used, it was only natural to feel anxious, right?

It was a world reminiscent of early modern Europe, but since the protagonist had to raise flags with the capture targets at the academy and complete reward events in various locations, there were vehicles that fit the narrative.
Really, what a twisted world!
"Hehe, leave it to me. The station in the Royal Capital is quite crowded, so should I put a collar on you to avoid getting lost?"
"Uh, no, I'll politely decline that..."
What kind of play is that?
If rumors spread in the Royal Capital before we even reached the academy, it would be a disaster.
After that, we switched from the carriage to the train at the neighboring territory, which had not been mentioned much in the story, and we finally arrived at the Royal Capital, Aetherdam.
When I parted ways with Sebas at the station, I felt unexpectedly lonely.
Sebas, who had served the Brave Family since I was born into this world, was almost like a parent to me after I lost my own.
It wasn't a farewell for life, as I intended to return home during the long break, but I couldn't hide my confusion at the homesickness that slipped into the gaps in my heart.
Thinking about it, Alicia, who had come to the Brave Family alone, seemed much more mature than I was.
"Wow, so this is the Royal Capital."
Thanks to my knowledge from the game, I knew what kind of city Aetherdam was, but I had no idea about the details outside the locations prepared for events.
That's why seeing the Royal Capital with my own eyes was amazing.
First, a gigantic dome-shaped protective barrier, symbolizing the magical nation, caught my attention.
This barrier was the masterpiece of the sage who founded the nation and had been protecting the Royal Capital for a long time.
To enjoy the peace and tranquility it provided, people flocked to the massive dome, resulting in a population that reached a million.
"Isn't the population density obviously insane?"
The buildings in the castle town were all at least three stories tall, densely packed together.
"That's why everyone loves to travel."
Alicia replied to my muttering.
People in the Royal Capital often traveled on their days off, and every time they returned, they would boast about where they had been, which was apparently quite annoying among the nobles.
I thought it was due to the story's need for events to unfold in various locations, but with such a dense and suffocating environment, it made sense.
"The area where the nobles live is still spacious, but compared to the Brave Territory, it feels cramped and uncomfortable."
"Well, comparing it to the Brave Territory is a bit much."
I had seen the neighboring territory on the way to the Royal Capital, and I felt a bit regretful realizing just how empty the Brave Territory truly was.
Still, this level of overcrowding felt excessive, even for a world designed for an otome game.
Well, if there was a long-standing guarantee of safety provided by the barrier, anyone would want to live inside it, leading to this situation, right?
It's twisted, it's twisted!
A shield that cannot be broken would be seen as a threat by foreign nations, which is why they conspire to wage war as a means of releasing pressure.
There seemed to be all sorts of issues lurking beneath the surface.
"But well, it doesn't seem like it would get boring."
"That might be true."
While attending the academy would be quite troublesome, I was genuinely excited because I had always admired cities in other worlds.
Even if it was an otome game world, it was still a city from another world, so I wanted to indulge in the delicious foods of this other world.
I quite liked B-grade gourmet food.
Right away, I caught a whiff of something delicious wafting from a stall outside the carriage window as we headed toward the academy.
"Grilled skewers? They look delicious."
"What are you talking about? The food in the Brave Territory was more than good enough."
"No, the meals I had were served with monsters looking completely unfazed."
"Oh, right..."
What a truly unique family I belonged to.
Some might think that the secret to our strength lay there, but it wasn't particularly different or that delicious, so I wouldn't recommend it.
If it were truly delicious, everyone would be eating monsters!

Just remembering the edible monsters and getting used to the idea of eating them would increase the chances of survival if we ever lost a battle and had to flee to places filled with monsters like mountains or forests.
I didn't know when it happened, but there was a lord of the Brave Family who had survived by sheer luck.
What a troublesome story.
"Lagna, do you have anything else you're looking forward to?"
"Hmm, I'm looking forward to the dungeon classes as well."
For some reason, there were dungeons within this protective barrier.
They were like ancient ruins left behind by the Ancient Sage, and the dungeons were used during practical magic classes.

It was a convenient dungeon prepared solely for the protagonist to encounter the capture target character in a crisis and overcome challenges together, but it was still a fairly authentic dungeon, so I was looking forward to it.
"Hehe."
Seeing me return to my childlike self, Alicia smiled.
"It looks fun."
"Of course, because I'm not alone."
How our school life would unfold from now on was already decided from the start.
A noble from the Discarded Land and a duchess who had been broken off from her engagement, right?
It was only natural to be looked down upon, and I had long since made up my mind about that.
At first, I lamented that it would be hell, but the former villainess sitting next to me was a truly stunning beauty.
We would simply play the role of side characters in the story, enjoying our school life as much as possible while trying not to get involved with the main characters.
"Oh, if there are any troublesome people, let me know right away, and I'll take care of it."
"Raising your hand is prohibited. You survived multiple wars and can even draw with a dragon, you know?"
As a collar was suddenly presented in front of me, I obediently went into my house.
I had thought about secretly intimidating any troublesome students, but if I got caught, I might really end up wearing that collar.
"Lagna, as long as you're here, I can handle anything that comes my way."
"Alicia, I think you're probably stronger than I am."
"That can't possibly be true."
I genuinely believed she excelled in everything except physical strength, but Alicia just laughed it off.
I knew well that very few people, even seasoned soldiers, possessed the mental fortitude to endure a hellish experience.
Let me briefly talk about the academy, the stage of our story.
The Aetherdam Academy, named after the country, gathered almost all the noble sons and daughters of this nation.
Those who were to inherit their families were forcibly enrolled, and even those who weren't could enroll without issue as long as they could pay the tuition and dormitory fees.

At this time, classes were divided according to titles and status, with those inheriting baron titles or higher, or earls and above, being placed in the upper class, while everyone else went to the lower class.
To put it simply, the upper class could potentially marry into the royal family, while the lower class could not.
Additionally, if a commoner was recognized for their special aptitude for magic or knowledge, they could enroll as an exception under the title of "Child of the Sage."
This was the so-called commoner slot, and they would be placed in the upper class without question, making it the protagonist's position in the otome game.
Since the things learned wouldn't change, I thought the lower class would be better since it would be less troublesome, but it seemed to be in accordance with the ancient sage's teachings.
It's vague and doesn't make much sense, does it?
Now, onto the main topic.
To be honest, there were only enemies in the upper class where Alicia originally belonged.
If possible, going to the lower class would be the correct route.
And if she went to the upper class, she would inevitably get caught up in the chaotic romantic comedy of the protagonists.
Even though it was the Discarded Land, I was a border count eligible for marriage into a duke's family.

In terms of status, I should have been placed in the upper class, but due to the rampant discrimination against the Discarded Land in the Royal Capital, I was fortunately confirmed to be in the lower class.
Alicia was also from a duke's family, but she was currently under the care of the Brave Family.
She had been treated so poorly that she couldn't even bring along servants, so she couldn't enter the special dormitory that required them, thus ending up in the lower class with me.
...Or so I thought, but when the lid was opened, it turned out we had somehow both been placed in the upper class together.
"This is strange! This is strange!"
"Stop it!"
As I banged my head against the desk, Alicia scolded me.
"This desk isn't as sturdy as your home!"
Furthermore, I had expected to be guided to separate dormitories, but for some reason, we were taken to an old mansion located a little away from the special dormitory.
"I'll endure whatever is said to me, so please don't act out of the ordinary."
"Understood. If I sense any danger in the girls' dormitory, I'll fly over."
"Stop it, you'll get expelled."
It was after we had made such a pact that things felt incredibly awkward.
There were no servants to supervise us, and we were forced to live under one roof. What kind of morals did this academy have?
"It seems Sebas has made arrangements with my family?"
"Eh, Sebas did?"
"When I arrived at this house, there was a letter left for me, and he wrote it."
The letter from Sebas stated the following:
As the Oldwood Duke's family, regardless of how much of a failure their daughter was, they would not allow her to move from the upper class to the lower class.
However, they also couldn't just send her back to school with servants as if nothing had happened, as that would lead to them being looked down upon by other nobles.
So, Sebas proposed this:
If she were to live her school life while enduring the shame, it would be seen as a proper measure by the duke's family, and other nobles would accept it.
In that way, it was decided to use this unused mysterious mansion as a substitute for the dormitory.
"It feels like I'm being treated like a pariah."
Alicia smiled with a troubled expression, but I could sense the kindness of her parents in that decision.
"This is a chance for redemption, isn't it? I think it's actually the most convenient option."
Living with the shame was a predetermined course, and it would be tough to be forced to have unreliable servants with us.
If I could maintain good grades in this current situation, I should be able to erase some of my failures.
"Plus, it makes it easier for me to protect you. I think it won't be much different from when we lived together."
Sebas really was something else for being able to solve the dormitory problem.
"That's true, right? I need to switch my mindset!"
After nodding several times, she slapped her cheeks to pump herself up.
"Shall we start by cleaning the room? It seems like it hasn't been used for a while, and it's dirtier than your house."
"Eh, do we really need to compare it to my place...?"
"Isn't it better than being compared to your room?"
"Eh?"
Did the servants of the Brave Family's habits rub off on her?
I didn't like that! I really didn't like it!
"It seems like the living essentials have already been moved in, so that's a relief. Lagna, I'll leave the heavy stuff to you."
"Okay."
Since there were other students in the dormitory, it seemed like there wouldn't be much time to breathe, so having a relaxing space was a significant improvement in the environment.
"Hey! There was a backyard here, right? Should we try growing vegetables here too? Nobody will come to check on it anyway, so it should be fine, right?"
"I think that's a good idea."
Hmm, she's become quite resilient.
As I watched Alicia, who was so different from when we first met, I gazed at the letter, and the magically written characters began to glow faintly.
This was the Brave-style magical script that could only be read with special training.
"──The contraceptives are hidden in the young master's room. Good luck."
Even in a letter, how annoying! Wasn't there anything else to convey?
As I thought it was a waste of paper, I noticed another message below.

"Young master, the only thing I managed to do was to have you both live together, and for you, who was originally scheduled to be in the lower class, you will need to take an exam to enter the upper class. The exam will be based on your abilities, so please do your best."
I see, I didn't know what kind of exam there would be, but if it was based on ability, passing it was what the bloodline of the Brave Family was all about.
That very day, I was called to the location where the exam for entering the upper class would take place.
The training building within the academy could be described as a gymnasium in modern terms.
Oh, it was written plainly on the sign as a gymnasium, so it seemed that was what it was.
In addition to practicing magic, classes like swordsmanship that involved physical activity were also held here, and along the indoor walls were a large number of wooden swords and striking dummies.
"There's no way this is a written exam."
I had been told to wear the academy's designated gym clothes, so I donned a green tracksuit meant for first-years and entered the gym.
N-No way, why is there a tracksuit in another world!? But I didn't feel surprised.
This was the Aetherdam Academy, the stage of the otome game, where all sorts of convenient narratives and contradictions flowed freely.
I could finally see Alicia in her tracksuit, a sight I had never seen in the game, so I had to give a thumbs up to the game developers.
I hadn't even seen her in her uniform yet, and I was looking forward to what was to come!
I had no interest in handsome guys in uniforms, bleh!
"Are you Lagna Vel Brave?"
"Yes, I'm Lagna."
"Don't keep the upper-class teacher waiting, you noble from the Discarded Land."
"I got lost since I had never been here before."
In the gym, a teacher with a rather high-handed attitude stood with his arms crossed.
"Tch, why do I have to be the examiner for this one...?"
He muttered loudly enough for me to hear.
Hmm, just as I thought, a negative start.
I was confident in my abilities, but as long as there was underlying discrimination, starting from a negative position would be difficult for anyone, no matter how hard they tried.
But well, if I was going to start from a negative, I might as well embrace it.
"I can hear you. So, shall we get this over with quickly?"
"Tch, don't talk back, barbarian."
If you want to finish quickly, you should just start without throwing insults, but he clicked his tongue again.
"First, we'll begin with a basic magic test. Shoot your maximum output at that target."
The examiner, holding a binder, pointed to a black monolith-like target made for anti-magic.
"Is there a specific type of magic I should use?"
"Tch, stop being so annoying. There's no specification, just do it."
Having been told that, I decided to get started.
"Alright, here I go."
As I responded, I casually struck the space in front of me.
Boom!
The impact shook the gymnasium, and the anti-magic target, which was about ten meters away, exploded into pieces.
The force continued unabated, creating a large wind hole in the sturdy stone wall of the stylish gymnasium.
It had been a while since I had gone all out since I punched the Onyx.
"How about that, teacher? Did I pass?"
"...Huh? What?"
When I turned around, the examiner was standing there, his clothes in tatters from the aftershock, looking dazed.
"Is that not enough? With that target's durability, it can't be measured... so, shall I do it again?"
"No, that's enough, that's enough!"
Though I was used to discrimination, it was still frustrating, so seeing the examiner panic made me feel a bit relieved.
This was just an exam, and I simply did what I was told.
By the way, if you were to ask what I did, I created a small barrier in front of me, punched it, and sent it hurtling at that target at supersonic speed.
I had learned all types of magic and could wield them with tactical-level power, but my specialty was barriers.
Oh, the Brave Family doesn't have a unique magic passed down through generations.
My father was good at body enhancement magic, and my two brothers excelled in healing and counter-magic, respectively.
Completely diverse and all basic elemental types that anyone could use.
"Well then, teacher, did I pass?"
"...The exam isn't over yet."
The examiner wore a face that looked like he had bitten into a bitter bug, as if he really didn't want to pass me.
I could tell there was a duke's family behind him.
"Now, let's move on to the next part. You want to finish quickly, right?"
"T-The next is the swordsmanship test."
"Swordsmanship in a magical nation?"

"That's right. If you look at the striking dummies over there, you'll understand, right? Even if you excel in magic, it means nothing if your body isn't strong. The academy incorporates this to build strong bodies. The sages were gods of magic, but they could also wield swords."
Did he think I couldn't use swordsmanship? The examiner became lively and started talking excitedly.
The protagonist had entered the upper class, but he wasn't particularly skilled with a sword, was he?
I could feel the determination that he absolutely did not want to pass me.
"If you can defeat me, you pass."
"Eh?"
"Both skills are essential for a noble. I can't allow someone who neglects one for the other to enter the upper class."
Was he overly confident, or was he looking down on me? The examiner brandished his wooden sword with bravado.
Meanwhile, I was so surprised that I couldn't even speak.
Did the examiner not know why the Discarded Land was called the Discarded Land?
Monsters appeared frequently, and wars happened often, which is why it was called the Discarded Land.
"So, I just need to... defeat you, right?"
"That's right. Using magic is prohibited; if you do, you'll fail immediately."
"Understood."
I took the wooden sword handed to me and got into position.
"Also, if you lose to me, you'll fail. I'll go all out for your sake, since you wish to enter the upper class."
"Ah, okay, feel free to come at me from anywhere."
"This!"
After quickly responding, the examiner charged in with a vein bulging on his forehead.
He must have had some skill to be so confident, but his movements were too linear and clumsy.
It was the kind of swordsmanship that someone who had never fought in a life-or-death situation would have.
"Haah! Gah!?"
I easily dodged and struck him on the temple, causing him to roll his eyes back and faint. He was too weak.
As the examiner trembled and began to lose control of himself, I took his wooden sword and snapped it in half, revealing that it had iron embedded inside.
"Ah, I knew it... I thought as much."
My wooden sword had broken when I hit him, and if I had been honest and fought him, I would have definitely failed.
People like him would say, "I can't fight because I don't have a weapon, so I fail!" after my sword broke.
Seriously, Alicia's prediction that they would try to expel me at any chance was spot on.
"Lagna Vel Brave."
As I was feeling exasperated, a voice came from the entrance of the gymnasium.
Looking over, I saw an elderly man with grayish-brown curly hair, sharp eyes like a hawk, and a long beard tied at his chest.
He was wearing a high-quality robe in a dull color, adorned with intricate details, and I recognized him.
His name was Volzeia Gran Cascade.
He was the headmaster of Aetherdam Academy and one of the men with the title of sage.
"I thought it was noisy; it was your doing."
"Yes, well..."
In this country, the middle name "Gran" was a sign of a duke's family, and the Cascade family was one of the three duke families in Aetherdam.
I knew this because this old man often appeared in the game.
He was depicted as a capable person who could declare that all nobles and commoners were equal as students of the sage within the academy founded by the great sage.
This game was a love story between nobles and commoners.
He was a character who subtly assisted the protagonists, troubled by their differences in status, within the academy.
"Hmm."
Looking at the shattered black target, the large hole in the wall, the fainting examiner, and the wooden sword with iron inside, Volzeia briefly stated.
"Pass."
"Thank you very much."
I sincerely expressed my gratitude.
Although Volzeia was a character on the protagonist's side, he seemed to have a flat perspective, as he didn't condone discrimination, even if I was from the Brave Family.
"I would like to ask you one thing... What magic can you use?"
"All of it."

In this magical nation, I could use all the most popular elements: fire, water, wind, earth, as well as sub-elements like ice and lightning, and the dualities of light and darkness, holy and evil, positive and negative, as long as I could remember them.
"And which one are you the best at?"
"Barriers. ──That's why I learned all of them."
To survive in the Brave Territory and to resist fate, I couldn't afford to miss even one. That's why I learned them all.
When I answered honestly, Volzeia stroked his beard slightly and seemed to ponder something before saying.
"Then you should be exempt from classes."
"Is that okay?"
"If your words are true, you cannot be measured by the foolish standards of others."
The "foolish" he referred to could be the examiner rolling his eyes, the idiots who only saw the surface, or the rotten ones who sat on their rights.
Volzeia's words seemed to carry various meanings.
